findings.detail: Research and writing artifacts are persisted under cloud_pilot/live_artifacts rather than the permitted daily research, articles, QA or deliveries paths. The writing packet also takes research_baseline_sha from the pre-research plan; it does not record the commit containing the completed research handoff as the writing baseline.
findings.required_fix: Persist the Fact Sheet, Source Log and handoff within the Research file boundary, push them and bind Writing to the actual research-completion commit. Store writing outputs within the permitted Writing paths and retain immutable versioning.

findings.detail: Engine.run retrieves or restores evidence before calling EditorialState.begin. A new evidence epoch can therefore be collected while the previous research head remains writable, contrary to the required lock-before-research and immediate stale-writer invalidation protocol.
findings.required_fix: Acquire the shared research lock and invalidate the prior head before any evidence refresh or transfer for that article. Keep the lock in force on retrieval failure and test the active Engine path during a concurrent update.

findings.detail: Research transitions and delivery are not atomic. Multiple pending research starts can select the same next version, and one can mark the head ready while another remains in progress. Separately, a research update can occur after a pre-delivery check but before a draft PR or localized artifact is created; the subsequent check fails only after the stale artifact exists.
findings.required_fix: Use an atomic, versioned lock/head transition with fencing for writing and delivery. Prevent or invalidate stale draft artifacts and PRs, and add interleaving tests covering concurrent research, writing, localization and delivery.

findings.detail: If registration writes research-current but stops before writing RESEARCH_READY, a retry sees the matching current row and returns without restoring the ready transition. The subsequent writing-lock check remains blocked by RESEARCH_LOCK, so the documented resume path cannot recover automatically.
findings.required_fix: Make head registration and readiness atomic or explicitly recover the incomplete transition. Add a crash-and-resume test between those checkpoints without resending a completed model request.

cloud-pilot-manual.yml.content:
name: AutoBridge multilingual API pilot
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      mode:
        description: Offline inspection or separately approved real execution
        type: choice
        options: [preflight, account-check, audit, execute]
        default: preflight
permissions:
  contents: read
concurrency:
  group: autobridge-entire-real-pilot-program
  cancel-in-progress: false
jobs:
  trusted:
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
    uses: xysjou/AutoBridge-Content-Pipeline/.github/workflows/cloud-pilot-trusted.yml@b3f5a6cef20b8dc235f001af306e635f1eca0fdf
    with:
      mode: ${{ inputs.mode }}
    secrets:
      OPENAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
      AUTOBRIDGE_CONTROL_COMMIT: ${{ secrets.AUTOBRIDGE_CONTROL_COMMIT }}
      AUTOBRIDGE_LIVE_APPROVAL_SHA256: ${{ secrets.AUTOBRIDGE_LIVE_APPROVAL_SHA256 }}

cloud-pilot-trusted.yml.content:
name: AutoBridge pinned protected runtime
on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      mode:
        type: string
        required: true
    secrets:
      OPENAI_API_KEY:
        required: true
      AUTOBRIDGE_CONTROL_COMMIT:
        required: true
      AUTOBRIDGE_LIVE_APPROVAL_SHA256:
        required: true
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  inspect:
    if: inputs.mode == 'preflight'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262
        with:
          ref: ${{ vars.AUTOBRIDGE_APPROVED_CODE_SHA || github.sha }}
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-python@a26af69be951a213d495a4c3e4e4022e16d87065
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'
      - run: python3 -m cloud_pilot.multilingual preflight
  account-check:
    # Availability is inspected inside the code/lease-preauthorized execute path.
    # Disable the legacy standalone key-bearing path permanently.
    if: ${{ false }}
    environment: autobridge-pilot
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262
        with:
          ref: ${{ vars.AUTOBRIDGE_APPROVED_CODE_SHA }}
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-python@a26af69be951a213d495a4c3e4e4022e16d87065
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'
      - name: Inspect only the two configured model metadata endpoints
        env:
          OPENAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
          AUTOBRIDGE_APPROVED_CODE_SHA: ${{ vars.AUTOBRIDGE_APPROVED_CODE_SHA }}
          AUTOBRIDGE_ACCOUNT_CHECK_APPROVED: 'true'
        run: python3 -m cloud_pilot.multilingual account-check
  execute:
    if: >-
      (inputs.mode == 'execute' || inputs.mode == 'audit') &&
      vars.AUTOBRIDGE_LIVE_ENABLED == 'true' &&
      github.ref == 'refs/heads/integration/work-cloud-pilot-m1-20261102'
    environment: autobridge-pilot
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 180
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262
        with:
          ref: ${{ vars.AUTOBRIDGE_APPROVED_CODE_SHA }}
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-python@a26af69be951a213d495a4c3e4e4022e16d87065
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'
      - name: Fetch reviewed control documents from a separate immutable commit
        env:
          AUTOBRIDGE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          AUTOBRIDGE_APPROVAL_COMMIT: ${{ secrets.AUTOBRIDGE_CONTROL_COMMIT }}
          AUTOBRIDGE_APPROVED_CODE_SHA: ${{ vars.AUTOBRIDGE_APPROVED_CODE_SHA }}
        run: python3 -m cloud_pilot.multilingual.control
      - name: Validate exact run and workflow lease before exposing the project key
        env:
          AUTOBRIDGE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          AUTOBRIDGE_LIVE_APPROVAL_SHA256: ${{ secrets.AUTOBRIDGE_LIVE_APPROVAL_SHA256 }}
        run: >-
          python3 -m cloud_pilot.multilingual preauthorize
          --plan "$RUNNER_TEMP/autobridge-approved/approved-plan.json"
          --prices "$RUNNER_TEMP/autobridge-approved/approved-prices.json"
          --permit "$RUNNER_TEMP/autobridge-approved/approved-permit.json"
      - name: Execute approved phase with the existing whole-program budget
        env:
          OPENAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
          AUTOBRIDGE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          AUTOBRIDGE_LIVE_APPROVAL_SHA256: ${{ secrets.AUTOBRIDGE_LIVE_APPROVAL_SHA256 }}
          APPROVED_RUN_MODE: ${{ inputs.mode }}
        run: >-
          python3 -m cloud_pilot.multilingual "$APPROVED_RUN_MODE"
          --plan "$RUNNER_TEMP/autobridge-approved/approved-plan.json"
          --prices "$RUNNER_TEMP/autobridge-approved/approved-prices.json"
          --permit "$RUNNER_TEMP/autobridge-approved/approved-permit.json"

articles.reason: The reserve covers a China-market 2024 Q05 PHEV, including a 125-series trim; the proposed task is to assess an identified 2026 China-market Q05 BEV as an urban sourcing candidate, including current listing and stock checks. The RHD guide mentions NEVO Q05 only as a Thai RHD prospect, while the Southeast Asia SUV article provides a country-by-country shortlist method rather than a Q05-specific buying decision. The different year and powertrain alone do not establish distinctness: keep the 2024 PHEV separate and verify the 2026 BEV's exact identity and availability independently before making factual claims.

The Aumark and Tianjin KR articles discuss reefer configuration, chassis/body/unit separation, and buyer checks; the fleet guide covers general commercial-truck procurement and acceptance criteria; the PDI guide covers generic vehicle condition and carrier handover. The proposed guide has a distinct buyer decision if it stays focused on defining and documenting performance acceptance for a completed refrigerated truck—such as agreed cargo and ambient conditions, sensor/data records, door-opening pattern, power modes, and acceptance responsibility—rather than repeating chassis or refrigeration-unit selection, generic PDI, or general fleet tender advice.
